title: The widow's mite (Mark 12:35–44)
hook: after warning against showy religion, he points to a widow's two coins

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was Shema, hear, and the two great loves. Your line was not far from the kingdom.

Beware, Jesus warns the crowd in the temple, of those who love to walk around in long robes, be greeted with respect in the marketplace, and get the best seats in the synagogue and the places of honor at dinners. They devour widows' houses, and for show they make long prayers. Moments before, he told a scribe he was not far from the kingdom, so this isn't every scribe; it's a kind of showing off. Then Jesus sits down across from the temple treasury, where people drop in their offerings, and he watches. Rich people put in large amounts. Then a poor widow walks up and drops in two tiny coins. Mark gives no sign that anyone else looked twice.
screen: `BEWARE THE LONG ROBES.` → `HE SITS AND WATCHES.` → `TWO TINY COINS.`

segments.voice: Jesus calls his disciples over. Look at her. In the King James Bible: "this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living." More, not in amount, but in what it cost. The rich gave from what was left over. She gave from what she needed to eat. Mark names the coins, two lepta, and translates for his readers: two make one quadrans, a small Roman coin the King James calls a farthing. It calls her two coins two mites, which is where our title comes from. Christians have read this story in two ways, and they fit together. Often it's a picture of true generosity: what counts is the heart and the cost, not the size of the check. It's why people still speak of giving their mite. But some readers notice where Mark put it: right after the warning about people who devour widows' houses. They hear a lament too: a widow giving her last coins to a temple whose leaders are eating up widows. Jesus doesn't stop her, and he honors her. He also sees the system around her. Either way, the one who noticed her was Jesus. Among the big givers and long robes, he sat still long enough to see two coins drop, and to know what they meant.
screen: `MORE THAN ALL THE REST.` · `OF THEIR ABUNDANCE; OF HER WANT.` · `TWO MITES, ONE FARTHING.` · `PRAISE, AND A LAMENT.` · then, large: `SHE OF HER WANT DID CAST IN ALL THAT SHE HAD.`

segments.voice: Let the last week pass by you slowly: who gave something quietly, at real cost, without anyone noticing, the coworker who covered a shift, a parent who went without, the neighbor who dropped off soup? Picture them, and the cost, and let yourself be the one who notices. If you pray, name each of them before God.
Lepta, the two tiny coins the widow gave, the smallest coins there were. Jesus says she gave more than all of them.
Your line: she gave all she had. Two coins, and he saw them. Day two hundred fourteen.

howItsDone: Christians often speak of giving their "mite" when offering what little they have, and churches frequently read this story when talking about giving, stressing the cost of a gift rather than its size.
